S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

patient_info.stressor_event: Major changes in working hours or conditions
patient_info.stressor: Gabriel’s warehouse introduced a new inventory system and shifted him from a predictable daytime routine into rotating early-morning and late-evening coverage, with fewer familiar coworkers and more pressure to train younger staff on unfamiliar procedures. He had always relied on structure, bilingual mentoring, church volunteering, and his garden to keep life steady, but over 5 months his stress-related maladaptive response to the changed work conditions spread into home routines, family interactions, and basic work reliability. The impairment became severe when he began missing scheduled responsibilities, withdrawing from long-standing community roles, and considering leaving a job that had been central to his identity for decades. After a safety meeting in which his supervisor documented repeated problems and encouraged medical leave paperwork, Gabriel sought psychiatric care through a community health clinic.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart—I'm missing shifts and church commitments, snapping at my family, and some mornings I just sit there in my work boots wondering if I can even face the place anymore.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I started coming apart within the first few weeks after the warehouse changed my hours and brought in that new inventory system; before that, I was keeping my routine and responsibilities together.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: The work changes are still going on, and I have not had a real break from the new schedule or its fallout yet.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My supervisor has documented problems with my reliability and talked to me about medical leave, and I have pulled back from church duties that people counted on me for.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about five months, ever since the new warehouse schedule and inventory system started.
